header.title: Frame
header.subtitle: place the text on the 8 axes -- the coordinates of the mind that made it
header.output: Morphospace (the frame read as a space texts sit in)
header.grain: passage-level (keyed by passage_id, NOT source_key -- the Seam-2 key)

pills.fidelity: PARTIAL -- golden path clean; corpus-wide drift (now caught)

header.status_line: Frame places a text on 8 axes; on Mark 16 it is clean -- 26 placements across 8 of 8 axes, all in-vocab. Its vocab renders LIVE from exom_axis_vocabulary (never hardcoded), which is why it is the calibration model. Honest limit: corpus-wide (39381 placements across many texts), 429 axis/value pairs drifted off-vocab WITHOUT a fit-or-extend candidate; the S163 drift-check now catches it. So: golden path clean, corpus drift named.

what_it_is: Frame reads a whole passage and places it on eight axes -- the coordinates of the mind that produced it: how it knows (epistemic-warrant), what it takes to be real (ontological-commitment), how it reasons (inferential-operation), what end it seeks (telos), its attitude (evaluative-stance), how it interprets (hermeneutic-posture), and the shape + terms of the ground<->world relation (r_topology, r_condition). The eight coordinates ARE the text's position in the Morphospace.
why_it_matters: A frame placement is what lets two texts be COMPARED as points in one space rather than argued about impressionistically. It is also where an absence shows: an axis a text does NOT engage (the not-engaged sentinel) is a real, coded fact -- a mind that never asks the ontological question is telling you something. The morphospace is the map convergence and divergence are read off.

how_it_works.the_method_does: one atlas-reader pass places the passage on each of the 8 axes onto the ESTABLISHED vocab (fit-or-extend: propose a new value if none fits), with a confidence per value, a membership weight where a real compound splits an axis, and an explicit not-engaged when the axis does not apply.
how_it_works.you_get_back: the 8-axis coordinate (a placement per axis-value) + any proposed candidates, joined to the passage.

pipeline_context.note: sibling terms glossed so the card stands alone.
pipeline_context.move: one small action a text makes (agent does an operation to something, with a result) -- the unit the pipeline codes.
pipeline_context.Decompose: the node that breaks a passage into moves; Frame (in Situate) runs alongside it.
pipeline_context.Situate: the parent node: attaches context to each move; Frame is its coordinates aspect.
pipeline_context.Morphospace: the output Frame feeds: the 8 axes read as a space; each text is a point, distances are comparisons.
pipeline_context.fit-or-extend: the vocab discipline (s2.1 = cast wide, do not pre-anchor): pick from the established values; if none fits, PROPOSE a candidate (never force-fit).
pipeline_context.the candidate log: atlas_frame_read_candidate -- where a proposed new value (or a probed 9th axis) is recorded for review.
pipeline_context.not-engaged: an explicit sentinel placement: this axis does NOT apply to this text (so zero is provably distinct from a missed read). NOT the same as the ontological value 'not-asserted' (a real placement).
pipeline_context.passage_id: the atlas's key -- Frame is keyed by passage_id, not source_key (resolve via text_checkout, the crosswalk from a text to its passages).
pipeline_context.Seam-2: the failure this card guards against: reading a text on ONE key while its data sits under a sibling key (a key-scatter false-negative). Frame's is passage_id, not source_key.
pipeline_context.vocab status: each vocab value is green (finalized) / candidate (proposed, fit-or-extend, live) / held (parked) / retired (removed). The drawer shows green + candidate.
pipeline_context.R1-R5: the atlas reader's coding rubric (Decision 201): R5 = exactly the 8 axes; R1-R4 govern how richly + honestly each placement is coded. Not a reliability grade.
pipeline_context.PI: the principal investigator (the researcher) -- who locks methodology calls.

how_we_grade_it.Fidelity: mechanical: does every placement value map to a LIVE vocab value, or (fit-or-extend) a logged candidate? A value that is NEITHER is silent drift.
how_we_grade_it.Cold Read: self-sufficiency: a blind reader judges whether the card explains itself.
how_we_grade_it.vs-Wild: does the atlas placement beat a naive reader given only the passage + 'place it on these 8 axes'? (owed).
how_we_grade_it.result_categories: INCOMPLETE / FAIL / PARTIAL (golden clean, corpus drift) / PASS.

the_method_clean.note: the 8 axes (definitions), each with its live vocab rendered from exom_axis_vocabulary (green = finalized, candidate = fit-or-extend, live). The card never hardcodes the lists.

axes.gloss: how the text KNOWS / grounds its claims
what it takes to be REAL / the kind of being it assumes
how it REASONS / the move from premise to conclusion
the END it is oriented toward / what fulfillment is
how it HANDLES / interprets its object
the SHAPE of the ground<->world relation
the TERMS / mode of that relation

field_contract.note: OPEN; the warrant + the reader's uncertainty

the_method_clean.live_vocab_rule: Frame is THE model for the live-vocab rule: axis + value render from exom_axis_vocabulary, so the drawer cannot go stale. The reader may propose a candidate (fit-or-extend), which must be logged -- the drift-check enforces that discipline.

the_method_applied.note: Mark 16 placed on the 8 axes (render-from-data). Each axis shows the coded value(s), whether it is the primary placement, confidence, the evidence snippet, and the value's live vocab status. Mark 16 spans 2 passages (its passage_ids), so an axis can carry two primary placements -- one per passage, not a duplicate.

out_of_domain.note: the out-of-domain Frame comparison (s2.14) is OWED, not shown: the atlas has NOT yet placed the Daodejing passage (0 placements). The 8 axes are text-agnostic and ready; the missing step is running atlas_frame_reader on TTC-CH1. Reported honestly rather than faked.

where_saved.plain: Placements save to atlas_frame_read_placement, keyed by passage_id (resolve the text's passages via text_checkout). The vocab lives in exom_axis_vocabulary (the live controlled set); proposed values live in atlas_frame_read_candidate. Read at passage grain, never by source_key.

honest_limits: CORPUS-WIDE VOCAB DRIFT. 455 distinct off-vocab (axis,value) pairs are written in placements but NOT in exom_axis_vocabulary; only 26 off-vocab values were logged as fit-or-extend candidates, so 429 are SILENT drift (a value written without its candidate). Frame's axis/value are free-text by design (fit-or-extend), so there is no DB CHECK -- the S163 drift-check (atlas_frame_vocab_drift_check.py) is the Layer-3 backstop that now catches this. Reconciling the drift (triage candidates into the vocab; backfill candidate rows) is the LIBRARIAN SB's job -- the Librarian owns the atlas reader and will own the vocab table + definitions (PI, S163); this drift-check hands it to them. (455 = 429 silent + 26 candidate).
GOLDEN PATH IS CLEAN. On Mark 16 all 26 placements map to a live vocab value (green or candidate); 0 silent drift. So the drift is on OTHER texts, not the worked example.
FRAME IS PASSAGE-LEVEL, not per-move. The grain rule intends per-move frame too (each move its own coordinates), but that needs Decompose to stamp passage_id per move; not populated yet.
vs-Wild is OWED: give a naive reader the passage + 'place it on these 8 axes' and compare to the atlas placement. Cold Read is owed on this card. Both are the next checks.
1997 of the candidate log's rows are 9th-AXIS probes (R4 completeness test), pending review -- an open question whether the 8 axes are collectively exhaustive.

Reading-SB owns: Cold Read + vs-Wild on this card, and the per-move frame decision (Decompose stamps passage_id per move).

leans_on: the morphospace / ordination method (a trait-space texts are points in; borrowed from morphology/ecology -- the Meadows/Alexander cross-domain lineage)
frame semantics (Fillmore) + the sociology-of-knowledge sense of a 'frame of mind'
the 8 axes derive from the R1-R5 reader rubric (Decision 201) + the S6 split of ground-world-relation into r_topology + r_condition (Decision 199)
fit-or-extend controlled vocab (s2.1 anti-pre-anchoring): the value set grows as cases demand, logged as candidates
foundation.how_we_arrived: the atlas evolution (engine07 -> the 8-axis 3-table design), the R1-R5 rubric lock, the CRT calibration sample, and the S163 drift-check that surfaced the corpus vocab drift.

research_view.decision_trail: Decision 199 (r_topology/r_condition split) - Decision 201 (R1-R5 rubric) - CONTRACT_situate_closed_open_grain_s162 (Frame closed/open/grain) - the S163 drift-check + this drawer.

fidelity.golden_path: PASS (Mark 16: 26 placements, all in-vocab green+candidate, 0 silent-drift)

fidelity.meta_line: Fidelity PARTIAL (2026-08-10, mechanical): on the golden path Frame is CLEAN (26 placements, all map to a live exom_axis_vocabulary value). Corpus-wide it DRIFTS: 429 silent-drift pairs (values written outside the vocab WITHOUT the fit-or-extend candidate). Frame's axis/value are free-text by design (fit-or-extend, s2.1), so there is no DB CHECK; the S163 drift-check (atlas_frame_vocab_drift_check.py) now makes the leak fail-loud. Reconciling the drift (triage candidates into the vocab; backfill missing candidate rows) is the owed work to reach corpus-green.
